subject: Budget constraint walkthrough & agreed action items (post-call)
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 17:02:00 -0400
Subject: Budget constraint walkthrough & agreed action items (post-call)

Hi Sarah — thanks again for your time just now. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps so we’re all aligned. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update the MAP.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Monthly inference budget capped at ~$48k (Q3 constraint) — procurement won’t approve more without clear TCO.
- Heavy peak usage at end of month (batchy bursts for reconciliation) causing unpredictable token spend and latency spikes.
- Need auditability (request for per-token logs / access controls) for security/compliance.

Goals we agreed on:
- 90-day pilot to validate 40–60% cost reduction on inference unit economics vs current provider for reconciliation pipeline.
- Maintain 99th percentile latency under 600ms for user-facing flows.
- Deliver a short TCO model that procurement can review within two weeks.

Proposed technical levers (we covered):
- Batching: small adaptive batching on reconciliation jobs + reserve burst capacity for end-of-month windows. Estimated token cost reduction: 20–30% (conservative).
- Prefix/KV caching: cache templated prompts and shared contexts for repeated reconciliation queries — expected additional 10–20% savings.
- Mixed precision / quantized variant for background jobs (non-user-facing) — up to 15% CPU/GPU cost savings depending on model choice.
- Smart routing: route sensitive low-latency traffic to dedicated T1 pool, route bulk batch work to cost-optimized instances.

Concrete next steps and owners:
1) Redwood: Deliver a one-page TCO summary + 90-day pilot scope and expected savings model by Tue 5/25 (owner: me). Attachment: redwood-econ-one-pager.pdf.
2) Ledgerly: Share a sample weekly usage CSV (tokens by route, peak windows) and the target SLAs for the UX flows by Fri 5/28 (owner: Sarah / procurement).
3) Infra/Eng sync: Karthik + Dylan to draft recommended instance sizing and batching strategy for reconciliation job and share runbook by Mon 5/31.
4) Procurement: If TCO model looks good, procurement to confirm procurement window and PO cadence; Redwood to provide required SOC2 artifact links and sample contract language (owner: Marissa).

Attachments included: redwood-econ-one-pager.pdf, ledgerly-map-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

If that aligns, I’ll start the TCO draft and loop in our legal/compliance docs for procurement. Thanks — talk soon.

—
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@ledgerly.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@ledgerly.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 17:38:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Budget constraint walkthrough & agreed action items (post-call)

Grace — thanks for the clear recap. That mirrors our internal notes. A couple quick clarifications before your TCO doc: 

1) Procurement will need a 90-day punch-list showing: estimated monthly token spend under Redwood, expected peak-day spend, and the delta vs our current vendor (we can provide the last three months of token usage).
2) We also need an estimated timeline for rollbacks/fallbacks in case latency objectives aren’t met during peak windows — procurement views this as a risk.

I’ll get the sample weekly usage CSV to you by EOD Friday. For the legal/compliance artifacts, procurement wants SOC2 Type II and a note on data retention — Marissa, can you start assembling those links?

Also: our head of infra, Tom Alvarez, asked whether the batch jobs can be scheduled into a dedicated low-cost pool with isolated data access (so logs don’t mingle with user-facing traffic). If you can include a recommended isolation approach in the runbook, that’ll help speed review.

Thanks — Sarah
SVP Product, Ledgerly
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 19:18:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Budget constraint walkthrough & agreed action items (post-call) — internal follow-ups

Looping you all on Sarah's confirmation and procurement asks. Action items for internal tracker: 

- Marissa: please pull SOC2 Type II link, sample contract redlines, and a short note on typical data retention options we present to customers (48–72 hrs vs 30/90 days). Put into the shared Drive link in related_links. Due Tue 5/25 COB.
- Dylan: focus on the runbook for isolated low-cost pool + fallback routing. Karthik to add sizing/quantization guidance. Aim for initial draft Mon 5/31.
- Karthik: include an example cost calc for quantized background jobs (assume 16-bit -> int8 path) and note any expected accuracy impacts.

I’ll draft the 1-page TCO and the pilot scope now and circulate for review before sending to Sarah. If anyone sees major risks we didn’t capture, call them out here.

—
Grace
